runningWorkouts.title: Introductory Acceleration Drive Builder Drill
runningWorkouts.summary: Structured 100m workout focusing on speed, acceleration, power, coordination.
runningWorkouts.riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 20m at target Maximum Sprint Speed intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 2 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 2 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 5 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 5 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Full recovery between sprints ensures maximal speed quality and reduces injury risk.
Emphasize explosive starts, rapid arm drive, and proper ankle stiffness.
Ensure full nervous system recovery; do not rush starts while feeling winded.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 800m at target 400m Race Pace / High Lactate Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 90s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown

Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment

notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 6 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 90s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: High lactate tolerance is developed by sustaining high-speed mechanics under muscular burn.
Manage the race distribution: accelerate smoothly in the first 50m, then float.
Focus on knee drive and loose shoulders over the final 100m.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

runningWorkouts.riskReason: Structured pacing ensures safe muscular adaptation. Maintain proper hydration and dynamic warmup.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: 5K REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 400m at target 5K Race Pace / VO2-style Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 4 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 5K REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 4 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 8 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 5K REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 8 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Raise the threshold and aerobic capacity with highly paced intervals.
Maintain specific goal 5K rhythm; do not over-speed on early reps.
Keep active recoveries moving at a slow but steady shuffle jog.
commonMistakes: Running too fast on recovery intervals, leading to premature workout fatigue.
Tensing the shoulders and neck during hard intervals, restricting breathing.
Neglecting proper dynamic warmup drills before starting high-velocity reps.
safetyNotes: Stay fully hydrated and check heart rate responses on hot or humid training days.
Halt execution immediately if experiencing any sharp joint or muscular pain.
Choose a flat, well-lit surface with clean traction for speed work.

runningWorkouts.riskReason: Structured pacing ensures safe muscular adaptation. Maintain proper hydration and dynamic warmup.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Marathon LONG-RUN Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 2000m at target Marathon Pace / Steady-State Aerobic intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 2 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 1 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Marathon LONG-RUN Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 1 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 2 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Marathon LONG-RUN Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 3 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 2 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Build marathon pace stamina, steady aerobic capacity, and fatigue resistance.
Keep the intervals strictly at target marathon pace (not faster).
Use float recoveries to teach the body to clear lactate at marathon effort levels.
commonMistakes: Running the tempo blocks too fast, turning an aerobic session into a race.
Skipping hydration/fuel practice on extended steady runs.
Starting the workout with insufficient carbohydrate fuel stores.
safetyNotes: Practice proper fueling and sodium replacement on runs exceeding 90 minutes.
Listen to physical fatigue signals on progressive volume long runs.
Wear premium running shoes with adequate structural support.

supportRoutines.title: Introductory Arm Drive Strength Primer Reset
supportRoutines.summary: Upper Strength session focusing on upper body strength, posture, arm drive.
supportRoutines.riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: Push-up
notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.
Keep the torso completely stable.
Execute each repetition with control.

sessionStructure.name: Dumbbell Row
notes: Maintain normal breathing cadence.
Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Incline Push-up
notes: Engage your stabilizer muscles.
Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Upper body strength supports running posture and efficient arm drive without adding excessive mass.
Focus on keeping the scapula retracting smoothly.
Complete all presses with complete control on the eccentric lowering phase.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

supportRoutines.summary: Upper Strength session focusing on upper body strength, posture, arm drive.
supportRoutines.riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: Push-up
notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.
Keep the torso completely stable.
Execute each repetition with control.

sessionStructure.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
notes: Maintain normal breathing cadence.
Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Single-Arm Farmer's Carry
notes: Engage your stabilizer muscles.
Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Upper body strength supports running posture and efficient arm drive without adding excessive mass.
Focus on keeping the scapula retracting smoothly.
Complete all presses with complete control on the eccentric lowering phase.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 2 to 1 to manage local muscular fatigue.

coachingNotes: Low-level pogos and line hops develop tendon elasticity and ankle stiffness.
Maintain stiff ankles upon contact, reacting off the ground quickly.
Always perform plyometric work on forgiving surfaces (grass, track, or mat).
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Perform all plyometric work on forgiving surfaces like turf or track.
Stop immediately if experiencing shin or knee pain.
Advanced depth drops require maximum focus; do not perform while heavily fatigued.

supportRoutines.title: Continuous A-Skip Running Mechanics Support
supportRoutines.summary: Running Drills session focusing on running form, coordination, efficiency.
supportRoutines.riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: A-Skip
notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.
Keep the torso completely stable.
Execute each repetition with control.

sessionStructure.name: Straight Leg Bounds
notes: Maintain normal breathing cadence.
Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Arm Swing Drill
notes: Engage your stabilizer muscles.
Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Drills develop running coordination, posture, and foot strike efficiency.
Stay tall, high chest, with arms driving dynamically from the shoulder.
Focus on a high-cadence quick midfoot contact.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

sessionStructure.name: Dynamic Leg Swings
notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.
Keep the torso completely stable.
Execute each repetition with control.

sessionStructure.name: Dynamic Lunges
notes: Maintain normal breathing cadence.
Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Butt Kick jogs
notes: Engage your stabilizer muscles.
Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Dynamic warm-ups prepare the muscle-tendon units and heart rate ranges.
Progress from low-velocity movements to faster dynamic drills.
Do not hold static stretches before high-intensity workouts.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

allEntries.title: Introductory Acceleration Drive Builder Drill
allEntries.summary: Structured 100m workout focusing on speed, acceleration, power, coordination.
allEntries.riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 20m at target Maximum Sprint Speed intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 2 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 2 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 5 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 5 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Full recovery between sprints ensures maximal speed quality and reduces injury risk.
Emphasize explosive starts, rapid arm drive, and proper ankle stiffness.
Ensure full nervous system recovery; do not rush starts while feeling winded.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

allEntries.summary: Structured 200m workout focusing on speed, speed endurance.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 120m at target Near-maximal Sprint Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 3 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Near-maximal REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 6 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 240s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Curve running requires progressive inward lean and rapid arm action.
Maintain speed rhythm as you transition out of the curve onto the home straight.
Recovery walking should be slow and deliberate to allow lactate dispersion.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

mainSet.name: 400m REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 150m at target 400m Race Pace / High Lactate Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 150s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown

notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 2 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m REPEAT Interval Segment

notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 5 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 5 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 150s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: High lactate tolerance is developed by sustaining high-speed mechanics under muscular burn.
Manage the race distribution: accelerate smoothly in the first 50m, then float.
Focus on knee drive and loose shoulders over the final 100m.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

allEntries.riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 400m at target 400m Race Pace / High Lactate Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 8 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 6 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 8 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 10 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 10 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 8 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: High lactate tolerance is developed by sustaining high-speed mechanics under muscular burn.
Manage the race distribution: accelerate smoothly in the first 50m, then float.
Focus on knee drive and loose shoulders over the final 100m.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 4 repetitions.

coachingNotes: Balance aerobic strength and raw speed to construct a complete 800m performance.

mainSet.name: 5K REPEAT Interval Segment

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

coachingNotes: Raise the threshold and aerobic capacity with highly paced intervals.

coachingNotes: Target climbing power, footwork control, and effort-based pacing over trail grades.
Ditch road pace targets; run purely based on subjective perceived exertion (RPE).

Watch for loose dirt, tree roots, and wildlife on the trails.
Carry proper trail hydration packs on remote routes.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Effort-Based FARTLEK Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 5000m at target Effort-Based Trail Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown

notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 4 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Effort-Based FARTLEK Interval Segment

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 8 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Effort-Based FARTLEK Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 8 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 6 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 120s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Target climbing power, footwork control, and effort-based pacing over trail grades.
Ditch road pace targets; run purely based on subjective perceived exertion (RPE).
Practice high cadence downhill stride patterns to minimize quadriceps fatigue.
commonMistakes: Trying to maintain road pace on steep climbs, resulting in early heart rate spikes.
Leaning backward on downhill runs, which increases knee stress and slip risk.
Neglecting trail surface changes, causing trips on hidden tree roots or loose rocks.
safetyNotes: Control downhill speed on technical grades to avoid slips and protect joints.
Watch for loose dirt, tree roots, and wildlife on the trails.
Carry proper trail hydration packs on remote routes.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 4 to 3 to manage local muscular fatigue.

coachingNotes: Low-level pogos and line hops develop tendon elasticity and ankle stiffness.
Maintain stiff ankles upon contact, reacting off the ground quickly.
Always perform plyometric work on forgiving surfaces (grass, track, or mat).
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Perform all plyometric work on forgiving surfaces like turf or track.
Stop immediately if experiencing shin or knee pain.
Keep jumps low-level and focus on quiet landings.

allEntries.summary: Running Drills session focusing on running form, coordination, efficiency.
allEntries.riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: A-Skip
notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.
Keep the torso completely stable.
Execute each repetition with control.

sessionStructure.name: Ankle Dribbling
notes: Maintain normal breathing cadence.
Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Arm Swing Drill
notes: Engage your stabilizer muscles.
Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 2 sets per exercise.
Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: Drills develop running coordination, posture, and foot strike efficiency.
Stay tall, high chest, with arms driving dynamically from the shoulder.
Focus on a high-cadence quick midfoot contact.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

coachingNotes: Dynamic warm-ups prepare the muscle-tendon units and heart rate ranges.
Progress from low-velocity movements to faster dynamic drills.
Do not hold static stretches before high-intensity workouts.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.

notes: Focus on precise movement alignment.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 2 to 1 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Run only 1 sets per exercise.

coachingNotes: Tissue durability routines build localized capacity and tendon resilience.
Control calf drops slowly to protect the Achilles tendon.
Execute single-leg knee controls carefully to maintain proper hip alignment.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.
